chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ismail ibn Mansur, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When four grandmothers gather, two from the side of the mother and two from the side of the father, one is discarded from the side of the mother by lot, so the one-sixth share is divided among the three. And similarly, when four grandfathers gather, one is discarded from the side of the mother by lot, and the one-sixth share is divided among the three.
ai.seo_question: How is the one-sixth inheritance share distributed among four grandmothers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the Shia jurisprudence of 'takhrij' (exclusion) among multiple grandmothers and grandfathers, specifically addressing the scenario where four grandmothers (two maternal, two paternal) or four grandfathers are present. It establishes that one maternal grandmother is excluded by lot (qur'a), leaving three to share the one-sixth (suds) portion, a ruling derived from the principle that maternal grandmothers take precedence over paternal ones in the absence of parents. This mechanism ensures equitable distribution among the 'three' remaining grandmothers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise application of the Quranic shares through prophetic tradition.
